notes:
Account snapshot - RAG/enterprise search for legal teams. Main focus on embeddings + reranking at scale; looking to replace brittle keyword search with vector + cross-encoder rerank.

Key requirements / constraints:
- Index scale: target ~40M documents initially, growing to ~120M across tenants. avg doc length 800-2,500 tokens. expect 6-10 vectors per doc (chunking).
- QPS/latency: target 200-300 sustained QPS at peak; 150ms p95 for user-facing search (includes ANN + rerank). reranker (cross-encoder) budget ~50-80ms p95 per query.
- Cost sensitivity: target cost per user query <$0.005 (embeddings+ANN+rerank amortized). strong interest in Redwood Optimize recommendations.
- Ingest: must support streaming ingest (near-real-time updates), S3 backfill, deduping, incremental reindex without multi-hour full reindexes. quote from CTO: "can't accept multi-hour reindex windows—legal discovery deadlines are real-time".
- Multi-tenant isolation: namespace-level quotas + per-tenant encryption keys (KMS).
- Connector requirements: native connectors or reference architecture for Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector (Postgres), Elastic vector extensions. Must provide:
  * high-throughput bulk ingest (10-30k vectors/sec sustained for backfill),
  * streaming ingest path with idempotency,
  * ability to set ANN index parameters per-tenant + hot-swap strategies,
  * metrics hooks for cost/latency per-route,
  * schema migration / versioning support.
- Reranking flow: dense-recall via ANN -> top-k (k=100) -> cross-encoder rerank. want Redwood to support automatic caching of dense candidates and configurable rerank thresholds to reduce cross-encoder cost.
- Preferred embeddings: open/hosted mix. experimenting with open embeddings (1536-dims) but want fallback to Redwood managed embeddings for SLA.

POC notes + results so far:
- 4M doc subset ingested to pgvector proof-of-concept. ANN recall decent but latency at 95th is ~240ms (above target) when rerank included.
- Weaviate + Pinecone tested as alternate backends: Pinecone gave best pure ANN latency but higher cost; Weaviate easier to self-host but ingest tooling maturity varies.
- Initial Optimize recommendations promising: prefix caching reduced repeated query cost by ~18% on dev set.

Risks / blockers:
- Legal requires clear data residency mapping per customer; on-prem offer must include audit logging and per-tenant KMS.
- Need connector ingestion throughput guarantees; current in-house pgvector path fails sustained backfill SLA.
- Cost modeling for rerank-heavy workloads uncertain—customer wants Redwood to model per-route costs including cross-encoder spend.

Sales notes / next steps:
- Deliver POC perf report by 2026-03-12 with breakdown: ANN latency, rerank latency, cost-per-query scenarios (k=10/k=100).
- Proposal: Dedicated nodes + VPC/private deployment + Optimize subscription; outline auto-scaling policy for bursts.
- Blocker to close: legal sign-off on data residency + connector SLA.
- Short-term ask from customer: sample connector repo for pgvector + Weaviate with streaming ingest example and metrics hooks.
